executiveSummary: GM0828 passes the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract. Its CBS/PDOK 2025 identity, 95,239-person municipality control, 106 neighbourhoods in 23 districts, 21 BAG places, 32 BRT settlements, three ProRail stations, 89 scheduled-transit stop areas and nine domestic NWB logical links are coherent; rounded neighbourhood rows sum to 95,270, only 31 above the separately published control (+0.033%). Release is nevertheless correction-required. Oss has a long, genuine Maas exposure from Lith through Oijen, Megen, Dieden, Keent and Ravenstein and current primary-dike programmes, yet the river preset reports exactly 2.014006 m from T+12 through T+72, 46,991 affected resident-equivalents at T+24 and 3,668,858.334 deprived person-hours at T+72 without selecting a Maas hydrograph, one of eleven contained LIWO primary candidates, defence/structure state, connected footprint, arrival or recession. Current Lith observations and requested forecasts are context only and stop short of a complete three-station T+48 and any T+72 horizon. Direct open-coast water is correctly zero and should remain suppressed in that narrow source scope, not become an all-clear for Maas, dike, polder, sewer, groundwater or pluvial pathways. Pluvial reports 0.215736 m at T+12/T+24 and Drainage availability 0.658119 at T+24 without using the official 2018 stress test, hydraulic sewer model, known/prioritised nuisance locations, groundwater, pumps or receiving-water state. Storm, pluvial, river, heat, winter, cyber and compound reuse the same resident-heavy leading five neighbourhoods. A controlled T+24 source at the official Koolwijk en Bossen centre produces direct fire 0.358612, smoke 0.450193 and 12,903 affected, but the containing neighbourhood ranks 60/106 by affected residents. Industrial/transient exposure is understated: Elzenburg has 140 residents but 340 businesses and 318 non-residential buildings, while official municipal evidence identifies a large pharmaceutical cluster, trimodal logistics and multiple business parks; no current workforce, freight, hazardous inventory, source term or plume is consumed. The sole N329 link across the Maas is sourced from NWB sections classified VDA (ferry) but modeled as a continuously available 150-unit regional road; official Maasveren publishes multiple distinct crossings, seasonal schedules and separate live-stremming context. A50 road and Ravenstein rail bridges, three stations, rural dike roads and external acute care are not event-time routed. Public context identifies 161 water/wastewater objects, three observations, fourteen partial forecasts, one Enexis planning sample, 168 antennas and 64 education locations, but none establishes complete live topology, flow, backup, staffing or restoration. Unknown, NoData, candidate catalogues, design cases, forecasts, registers and published schedules must never become zero, safe, open or operational.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0828 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, settlement and safety-region context
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated snapshots retrieved 31 August–2 September 2026
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM0828 as Oss in Noord-Brabant and safety region Brabant-Noord and report 95,239 residents, density 588/km², 21.3% aged 65 or older and 15,812 one-person households; the generated centre [5.5261037274951965,51.77947198626351] lies inside the 2025 boundary.

One hundred six neighbourhood rows in 23 districts sum to 95,270 residents, 31 above the separately rounded municipality control (+0.033%); households sum to 43,430 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 20,265. Allocation reconciles to the control without rewriting published rows.

BAG supplies 21 places from Berghem and Oss through the dispersed Maas settlements; BRT supplies 32 source-labelled settlements: nineteen woonkernen, nine buurtschappen, two deelkernen and two gehuchten. No generated BAG place centre falls outside the generalized boundary.

All 36 CBS fields are exposed. District heating and charging are null in all 106 rows, cars per household in 30 and several housing/benefit/distance fields in 8–18 rows; null/suppression remains NoData. CBS/PDOK is CC BY 4.0 and BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Aa en Maas / Meanderende Maas / Gemeente Oss
evidenceSources.title: E02 — Ravenstein–Lith and Lith–Bokhoven primary-dike programmes
evidenceSources.edition: Current project pages inspected 3 September 2026; Meanderende Maas target year 2030
supports: Meanderende Maas combines strengthening of more than 26 km of Brabant dike between Ravenstein and Lith with river widening along an 18 km Maas reach; ten organisations work toward a stated 2030 result.

The Lith–Bokhoven page at https://www.aaenmaas.nl/in-jouw-buurt/projectenkaart/dijkverbetering-lith-bokhoven-dijk/ says the dike from Lith lock to Bokhoven must meet newer standards and is in an investigation/design-choice phase.

The Cuijk–Ravenstein page at https://www.aaenmaas.nl/in-jouw-buurt/projectenkaart/dijkverbetering-cuijk-ravenstein/ identifies one of the higher-consequence Maas trajectories and planned improvement upstream of the municipal boundary. This is a cross-boundary hydraulic/defence dependency.

Future-standard non-compliance, strengthening work and target dates are planning/project evidence, not an event-time failure, breach, construction state or consequence forecast. No blanket machine-reuse licence or live component-state feed was identified on the pages.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — LIWO 2025.1.6 Maas candidates and current Lith Waterinfo observation/forecast context
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO application 2025.1.6; WFS and Waterinfo deployment snapshots queried 2–3 September 2026
supports: The bounded query returns eleven primary and zero regional candidates, and point-in-polygon against the generated generalized boundary contains all eleven: Alem, Alphen, Dieden, Gewande, two Keent, Lith, Maas km 205, Maas km 207, Oijen and Waal. Administrative containment across boundary water requires authority association review.
Candidate points, dike-ring/open-water ids and frequency flags are scenario-selection metadata, not active failures, forecasts, connected footprints, metre depths, arrival or safe-state evidence.

Three fresh 2 September observations report Lith village/lock-below 47 cm NAP and Lith-above 489 cm NAP at 17:30Z. Fourteen requested forecasts cover three points at T+1/6/12/24 and only two at T+48; no T+72 feature exists.

Observations/forecasts require issue/valid time, location, parameter, unit, datum and quality and are not automatically the exercise hydrograph. Missing point/horizon combinations remain NoData. Waterinfo is CC0/non-mission-critical; LIWO release/licence and authority approval must remain attached.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Water- en Rioleringsprogramma Oss 2023–2029 and local water-nuisance mechanisms
evidenceSources.edition: Water- en Rioleringsprogramma 2023–2029, dated 25 October 2022; current public programme
supports: The programme separately governs urban wastewater, runoff/rainwater, groundwater, surface-water quality/quantity and drought, and links municipal systems to Aa en Maas treatment and water management.

It records a 2018 climate stress test and hydraulic sewer calculation, a prioritised list of locations informed by experienced nuisance, and measures at Oijen, Oss and Ravenstein. Some higher-priority locations were still between design and implementation when published.

The municipal water-nuisance page at https://www.oss.nl/inwoners/bouwen-en-wonen/Riolering/Wateroverlast.htm explains that many neighbourhoods use combined sewers which can fill during extreme rain, with street storage, building effects, local infiltration, ditches/ponds and blocked gullies as distinct mechanisms.

Programme and public guidance are static governance/design evidence, not event rainfall, current sewer/pump/gully/groundwater/receiving-water state or a completed measure. No standard redistribution licence or machine stress-test API was identified.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Aa en Maas / Gemeenten Oss, Bernheze and Maashorst / Veiligheidsregio Brabant-Noord / Staatsbosbeheer
evidenceSources.title: E05 — Official De Maashorst nature-fire management plan and source eligibility
evidenceSources.edition: Official plan announcement, signed 25 February 2026; page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Oss is one of six partners in the nature-fire management plan for De Maashorst, together with Bernheze, Maashorst, Aa en Maas, Staatsbosbeheer and VRBN. The plan has a dynamic implementation component and focuses on preventing fires becoming uncontrollable.

The authority explicitly connects water conservation and drought reduction in wet nature with reducing nature-fire probability, establishing a water–drought–fire interaction rather than a generic municipal scalar.
The audit-controlled source uses the official Koolwijk en Bossen neighbourhood centre as a bounded synthetic probe near the eastern nature context; it is not an observed incident or forecast.

Official plan/land-context evidence establishes eligibility and governance only, not current fuel moisture, ignition, perimeter, wind/plume, visitors, access, extinguishing-water availability, crew or suppression. No standard machine reuse licence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Industrial, pharmaceutical, trimodal-logistics and external-safety context
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal and national/provincial pages inspected 3 September 2026; CBS 2025 business/building statistics
supports: The municipality lists Elzenburg/De Geer, Vorstengrafdonk at A50/A59 and multiple other business parks. Its logistics page describes Oss as trimodal across road, water and rail.

The municipal pharma page at https://www.oss.nl/Tonen-op-pagina-standaard/Oss-waar-farma-floreert.htm identifies Organon, Aspen Oss, Pivot Park and other pharmaceutical research/production activity. Static sector/site descriptions do not establish dangerous substances or an incident.

CBS 2025 assigns Elzenburg 140 residents, 340 businesses and 318 non-residential buildings; Vorstengraf has 80 residents, 80 businesses and 36 non-residential buildings. Resident weighting cannot represent time-varying workers, freight or visitors.

The authoritative Register Externe Veiligheidsrisico's is described at https://iplo.nl/thema/externe-veiligheid/register-externe-veiligheidsrisico/ and the province's risky-company page points to Seveso/OMWB governance. The simulator consumes neither a current REV inventory nor a selected source term, site boundary, plume or protective action; absent matches must remain Unknown rather than safe.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Road, ferry, rail, scheduled-transit and external acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail snapshot and GTFS v9543 valid 30 August–12 December 2026; Maasveren schedule inspected 3 September 2026; RIVM acute care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: Nine NWB logical links reduce to A50, A59, N324, N329 and N277 physical identities. The sole GM0828–GM0668 N329 edge uses source sections NWB-600440814/600440815 with road-part class VDA (ferry), yet is modeled as a 150 scenario-unit regional road.

Maasveren publishes distinct Megen–Appeltern, Maasbommel–Megen, Alphen–Oijen and Lith–Alphen crossings with seasonal/day-specific hours and directs users to separate current stremming information. A recurring timetable is not scenario-time sailing, queue, priority, accessibility or throughput.

ProRail assigns Oss, Oss West and Ravenstein stations and GTFS 89 stop areas. Static station/stop/schedule geometry does not establish passenger counts, accessible rolling stock, actual operation or Ravenstein rail-bridge continuity; the road graph also does not model the A50 Maas bridge as a typed bridge asset.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 is CC0 and assigns no respondent acute point inside GM0828. Nearest centre-distance sites are 24/7 Bernhoven Uden (12.96 km), Rivierenland Tiel (14.39 km) and Jeroen Bosch (20.12 km); distance is not route time, ambulance state or acceptance. NWB is CC0; schedule/operator licence was not identified.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Aa en Maas / Brabant Water / Netbeheer Nederland / Enexis / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public water-chain, electricity, communications and education context
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; current authority project pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Generated containment assigns 161 HWH objects: nineteen sewer pumps, thirteen surface-water pumps, one wastewater treatment plant, two sluices and 126 weirs. HWH IMWA/DAMO is contributor-dependent/partial, weekly where supplied and CC BY-SA 4.0; register presence/type/capacity is not connectivity, live state, backup or restoration.

Aa en Maas says RWZI Oijen receives daily wastewater from approximately 300,000 residents and businesses in Oss and surroundings and discharges via Teefelse Wetering toward the Maas. The stamriool page at https://www.aaenmaas.nl/in-jouw-buurt/projectenkaart/renovatie-stamriool-oss/ identifies a 4.5 km main connection carrying Oss and surrounding cores to Oijen. Published project/catchment figures are not live flow, reserve or condition.

One NBNL sample maps to Enexis OS Oss and reports 150.8/142.1 MW existing/required withdrawal, a 45 MW/151-request withdrawal queue, 132.4/131.3 MW existing/required injection, a 12.7 MW/57-request injection queue and nineteen projects with earliest year 2026. These are planning values, not live load/outage/switching/reserve.

RDI assigns 168 antenna sites—73 mobile, 55 fixed-link, 26 amateur, eight broadcast and six other mobile—and DUO 64 education uses—30 primary, four secondary, eight special and 22 other. Brabant Water provider context, points and registers do not establish drinking-water zones/pressure/quality, connectivity, current occupancy, signal, shelter role or restoration. Exact NBNL reuse licence was not identified; RDI/DUO source terms and validity must remain attached.

evidenceSources.title: E09 — Regional risk governance and Oss first-72-hour water-outage preparedness exercise
evidenceSources.edition: Current VRBN story and Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2024–2027 inspected 3 September 2026
supports: VRBN documents an Oss/Ruwaard community exercise explicitly asking what residents would do if no tap water were available for 72 hours, focusing on self-help, mutual assistance, local skills/resources and neighbourhood connections.

The Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2024–2027 is publicly listed at https://vught.bestuurlijkeinformatie.nl/Agenda/Document/8f5ac0ef-c66f-4936-bcc2-145544193b9b?agendaItemId=bfbefd0a-aa22-4e86-b926-26d144a6f5bb&documentId=6aeecb71-cd8b-4c94-b0ea-0b1830b47313 and provides regional scenario/governance context, not activation or municipality-specific performance.
A preparedness discussion is not evidence that every household has water, medication, charging, transport or a helper, and it is not a current outage/resource observation.

No complete public machine feed for warning, evacuation, dike/pump/ferry/bridge decisions, shelter, care acceptance, industrial protective action, resupply, dewatering or utility restoration was identified; no blanket redistribution licence was found.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent river/compound disruption and all recovery labels lack accountable Oss actions, resources, access and operator evidence.
notes: River stays at 2.014006 m from T+12 through T+72; affected rises from 46,991 at T+24 to 50,811 at T+48/T+72, while seven service values freeze from T+24 and Facilities worsens at T+48 then freezes.
Compound reaches 47,880 affected and all eight services become numerically identical from T+48 through T+72 while remaining degraded; no action/resource state explains the plateau.

Other presets recover exactly without an owner, inspection, ferry/bridge/rail state, crew, equipment, fuel/water, care transfer, industrial clearance, completion observation or complete valid T+72 forecast.

findings.summary: Generated identity, settlement membership and 2025 demographic controls are coherent.
findings.evidence: GM0828, Oss, Noord-Brabant, Brabant-Noord and editions agree; centre is contained. CBS reports 95,239 residents; 106 rows total 95,270 (+0.033%) and reconcile without rewriting observations. Twenty-one BAG places and 32 BRT settlements are present.

findings.evidence: District heat/charging are null 106/106 and cars per household 30 times. There is no internal RIVM acute point, KNMI station/seismic origin, RIVM air point or NDW situation. Lith forecasts omit one T+48 point and all T+72 values. No value is fabricated.
findings.action: Preserve publisher/version, issue/valid time, spatial coverage, licence, NoData mask and reason code through ingestion, UI and export; absence never means zero, open, operational or safe.

findings.summary: A genuine Maas pathway is converted into unsupported exact persistent local inundation.
findings.evidence: River T+12 through T+72 reports exactly 2.014006 m, 46,991 affected at T+24 and 3,668,858.334 deprived person-hours at T+72. Eleven contained primary candidates and current Lith observations/partial forecasts exist, but no exercise hydrograph/datum, dike/structure state, selected case, connected footprint, arrival, velocity or recession is used.
findings.action: Retain Maas eligibility but gate exact magnitude, exposed population and consequences as Unknown until RWS/Aa en Maas select one versioned connected hydraulic/defence scenario. Keep direct North-Sea coastal water zero only in that narrow source scope.

findings.summary: Generic pluvial precision omits Oss's stress test, hydraulic sewer model, groundwater, pumps and receiving-water state.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+12/T+24 reports 0.215736 m and T+24 Drainage availability 0.658119 without selecting the 2018 climate stress test/hydraulic calculation, priority nuisance locations, combined/separate sewer and gullies, groundwater, 161 partial water assets or Maas/local-water boundary. The WRP explicitly separates these pathways.
findings.action: Ingest a governed Oss/Aa en Maas/AHN/GWSW event package with rain amount/duration, terrain, groundwater, sewer/gully inclusion, receiving-water boundary, controls, footprint/depth, arrival/recession, issue/valid time, units, CRS/resolution, licence, uncertainty and NoData.

findings.summary: Seven unrelated active hazards reuse the same first-five neighbourhood order.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, heat, winter, cyber and compound rank Berghem-Zuid, Berghem-Noord, Geffen, Centrum-West and Lith first through fifth despite incompatible mechanisms; Maas/dike/polder, stress-test and industrial areas are not source-selected.

findings.action: Keep canonical remote smoke labelled as such and add a named source-contained nature-fire exercise using eligible vegetation, current fuel/moisture, event-valid wind, visitors, access, extinguishing water and authority perimeter/suppression. findings.summary: Resident weighting understates industrial/pharma/logistics exposure and no governed hazardous-release pathway exists.
findings.evidence: Elzenburg has only 140 residents but 340 businesses and 318 non-residential buildings; Vorstengraf has 80 residents/80 businesses. findings.summary: An NWB ferry is misrepresented as a continuous regional road while other Maas crossings, rail/bridge state and external acute care are absent.

findings.summary: Public water assets, Oijen catchment figures and planning samples cannot support exact eight-service topology or restoration.

Reconcile public assets explicitly; keep sensitive/unavailable topology Unknown or the smallest transparent synthetic fallback.

findings.summary: Weather, heat/drought, winter, cyber, seismic and coastal consequences lack local event fields and support boundaries.

Earthquake T+6 reports 0.002846 g without named origin, ShakeMap, soil/site response or fragility. Direct coastal water is zero, but Maas/polder/local water remains separate Unknown.

findings.summary: The complete deterministic numerical, causal, allocation and checkpoint contract passes for GM0828.

Outputs are finite/deterministic; zero-event behaviour is exact; allocation/demand/delivery reconcile; causal arithmetic closes; burden is monotone; layer selection is invariant; and persistent modeled river water blocks generic recovery.

residualLimitations: This artifact audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a forecast, warning, evacuation instruction, hydraulic assessment, ferry/bridge/rail decision, hospital status, industrial release assessment or operator restoration commitment.

CBS 2025 values are rounded/suppressed and residents exclude industrial/pharma workers, freight/ferry/rail users, pupils, patients/staff, nature visitors, responders and displaced people; no timestamped dynamic occupancy is consumed.
Generalized polygons and centroids cannot resolve Maas floodplains/compartments, dikes/structures, polders, sewers/groundwater, combustible vegetation, industrial sites, crossings or utility zones.

Eleven contained LIWO points are candidates, not breaches or footprints. Generalized administrative containment across river water may associate opposite-bank candidates and requires authority review.
Lith observations/forecasts are valid-time context, not the selected exercise hydrograph. One T+48 point and all T+72 features are missing and remain NoData.

Future-standard dike work and the 2030 Meanderende Maas target do not mean event-time failure. Construction, temporary geometry and component condition can change and remain Unknown without a valid feed.
Municipal WRP/stress-test/hydraulic evidence establishes duties/design cases, not a live rain event, groundwater field, sewer/gully/pump state, completed measure or local depth.
The controlled nature-fire source is synthetic. Official plan context does not establish fuel moisture, ignition, perimeter, wind/plume, occupancy, access, extinguishing water, crew or suppression.

Business, pharma and logistics pages plus CBS counts do not establish current workers/freight, dangerous substances, source term, plume, site state or protective actions. REV/permitted data needs valid-time authority review.

NWB VDA proves a ferry-type section, not current sailing or capacity. Maasveren schedule is recurring context and separate stremming status is required; other crossings and A50/rail bridges need typed assets without double counting.
ProRail/GTFS are static/register/schedule evidence. Stations/stops do not establish passengers, accessibility, train/bus operation, bridge continuity or emergency role.

Zero internal RIVM acute-care respondent points does not erase local care/demand. Centre distance to external hospitals is not route time, ambulance availability, acceptance, beds, staff, utilities or backup.

HWH coverage is partial/provider-dependent; RWZI/stamriool public figures are catchment/project context. Neither establishes connected live topology, compatible flow, reserve, backup, control or recovery.

One NBNL sample, RDI antennas, DUO schools and absent local air/weather/NDW points are planning/register/coverage context. They do not establish customer connectivity, occupancy, load, signal, air surface, road state, reserve or repair.
The Ruwaard 72-hour no-tap-water workshop is preparedness/governance evidence, not proof of household supplies, mutual-aid availability or distribution performance.

Complete physical electricity, gas, drinking-water, wastewater, telecom, care, supply, crossing and emergency-resource topology/live state may be unavailable or security-sensitive and remains Unknown or explicitly synthetic.

Exact hazard, neighbourhood, affected-population, service-availability, recovery and person-hour values remain synthetic/derived screening until critical/high findings are corrected and authorities review the selected event; impacts beyond T+72 are outside scope.
